title: Frugal Inference Ops: Roadmap & Sprint Epic for Cross-Team Cost Engineering
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: deliver a coordinated roadmap and sprint epic that engineers, infra SRE, and product can execute to capture 12-20% unit-cost savings across hosted and dedicated deployments by combining dynamic batching profiles, adaptive KV-prefetching, and targeted quantization profiles.

Scope:
- Define per-route dynamic batching policy templates (latency-first / cost-first tiers).
- Implement adaptive KV prefetch heuristics that increase cache hit rate for common prompt prefixes and conversation sessions.
- Produce a catalog of per-model quantization profiles (8-bit, int4 candidate sets) with regression guardrails.
- Build savings-attribution dashboard and rollout playbook (canary -> regional rollouts -> A/B).

Success metrics / OKRs:
- O1: Reduce average per-token hosted cost by 18% for top-10 production routes (measurement in billing-unified view).
- O2: Increase KV cache hit rate from baseline to >= 35% on targeted routes.
- O3: Keep p99 generation latency within 10% of current SLO on any route where batching/quant is enabled.
- O4: Automate rollback on quality regressions with integrated eval runs and alerting.

Trade-offs & constraints:
- Quantization introduces quality risk — require per-model evals and a staged gating framework.
- Aggressive batching reduces GPU utilization variability but can increase tail latency for low-concurrency routes; therefore we will implement per-route latency guardrails.
- Prefetching increases memory usage and slightly higher throughput; we will cap heuristics based on per-pool memory budgets.

Milestones & timeline:
- M1 (Sprint 1): Prototype dynamic batching templates + infra feature flag (ENG spike) — owner: Marcus Kim — due 2026-03-01.
- M2 (Sprint 2): KV prefetch prototype + cache instrumentation + lightweight SLA tests — owner: Olivia Chen (SRE) — due 2026-03-28.
- M3 (Sprint 3): Quant profile evaluation pipeline + candidate profiles for 3 open models — owner: Applied ML — due 2026-04-15.
- M4 (Sprint 4): Savings dashboard v1, canary rollout plan, and runbook — owner: PM / DX — due 2026-04-30.

- PRD: https://confluence.redwoodai.com/display/FRUG/Frugal+Inference+Ops (draft)
- Experiment grid (spreadsheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1frugal-grid
- GitHub prototype PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4837, https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4859
- Savings dashboard (internal): https://app.datadog.com/dash/redwood/savings-attribution (alpha)

Review feedback & approvals:
- 2026-02-20: Design review (Diego Reyes) recommended a minimal UX for toggling per-route cost tier in Console; follow-up task created to spec Console change.
- 2026-03-03: Applied ML raised concerns about hallucination rate drift under int4 for one model; agreed to gate quant on automated eval pass and shadow traffic.
- 2026-03-10: Security asked for KMS-integrated key access when storing quant artifacts; security review items tracked in dependencies.

Risks & mitigations:
- Quality regression: require integrated eval harness and automated rollback on metric degradation.
- SLO breach: per-route latency guardrails and canary ramp limits.
- Billing attribution noise: implement unified attribution pipeline in savings dashboard and tag events with route/model/quant/batch-profile.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finish ENG spike for batching policy selectors and deliver feature-flagged implementation (Marcus).
- Add per-route cost-tier toggle to Console MVP (Design + DX).
- Run two customer-facing A/B pilots with controlled rollouts by 2026-04.

Stakeholders: PM (Nora Patel), Product Lead (Aisha Kapoor), Eng (Marcus Kim), SRE (Olivia Chen), Applied ML (Diego Reyes), Developer Experience (Leah Morgan).
